top_choice_rationale: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a mature, independently confirmed reaction class. Buchwald and Hartwig developed it in parallel, so a two-name allocation needs no forced omission. Making C-N reductive elimination from palladium amido complexes work through ligand design is a different mechanistic problem from the C-C transmetalation chemistry honored in 2010, and a citation worded 'general' and 'ligand-controlled' handles the Kosugi/Migita precursor. Targeted protein degradation (P002, then P003) is the next most novel, but no degrader is approved and the PROTAC and glue strands make the allocation a compromise; sequencing (P004) is arguably genomics, and lipid nanoparticle credit (P005) is too diffuse.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile (Lund colleagues Linke and Sparr are on the committee, but no specific tie to any proposal's laureates)
